reasoning: Both attempts have sound designs with per-player keys, ready handshakes, and removeClient on leave. B is written against the verified Charm 0.11.1 API (Charm.signal getter/setter) and vide-charm's useSignalState. A relies on Charm.atom and VideCharm.useAtom, which don't match the confirmed APIs and would likely break both placement and the UI at runtime. B is the safer, mergeable attempt.

criteria.note: PlayerState.get creates one `Charm.atom(MAX_BLOCKS_PER_PLAYER)` per player, the check reads `blocksLeft()`, and PlayerRemoving clears it; but `Charm.atom` is not part of Charm 0.11.1's verified signal API.

connect is called once and fires `remote:FireClient(player, payloads)`; keyAtoms builds per-player keys `{field}:{userId}`, subscribes on ready, and calls removeClient on leave. All correct if atoms work as getters.
PlayerSync.client calls addSignals with keyed atoms before connecting OnClientEvent → client.patch, then fires the ready remote.

`VideCharm.useAtom(PlayerState.blocksLeft)` runs inside the mounted app, which is not the verified `useSignalState` API; the server syncs the remaining count and the label stays hidden while it is nil, which is sensible.
Adding a field to both PlayerState modules is all it takes; keyAtoms handles the keys generically.
Checks pass, but relying on `Charm.atom`/`useAtom` against Charm 0.11.1/vide-charm 0.4.1 would likely break placement and the UI at runtime.
Each player gets `Charm.signal(PlayerData.Default)`, `update` replaces the table via `table.clone`, the check reads `data.BlocksPlaced`, and onPlayerRemoving clears the state.
connect is called once and fires syncRemote to the player; addSignalsToClient uses `PlayerData.syncKey(userId)` on ready; removeClient runs on leave.
addSignals registers setData under the same key, then connects OnClientEvent → patch before `readyRemote:FireServer()`.
`useSignalState` runs inside app; the limit is shared in BlockTypes.MaxBlocksPerPlayer; the default data shows 50 left before the first sync.
Only CharmSync calls setData; the UI just reads it.
Adding a value means adding a field to the PlayerData type and DEFAULT; it syncs under the same per-player key.
Correct against the verified APIs and all checks pass; the HotbarLayout refactor and absolute positioning add a little extra.

strengths: Clean per-field state modules on both sides
Ready handshake avoids losing the first payload
Label hidden until the count is known; stacked layout above the hotbar
weaknesses: Uses Charm.atom and VideCharm.useAtom, which don't match the verified Charm 0.11.1 signal / vide-charm useSignalState APIs
`:: any` casts hide the type mismatch

strengths: Uses the verified Charm.signal and useSignalState APIs
Shared limit constant; ready handshake; handles players already in game
weaknesses: Shows the default 50 before the real sync arrives
